frame_69017fe037bf.question: Vulnerability analysis of FeeBuyback
artifact_refs: Whether submit permits price manipulation through unvalidated swapData or arbitrary aggregator execution
Whether the full TEL balance can be exchanged at an attacker-controlled or economically unfavorable price
Whether referral, safe, and output-token handling lacks minimum-price, slippage, deadline, or oracle safeguards

history.rationale: WHY NOW: FeeBuyback is an unvisited critical component that sends the entire TEL balance and caller-provided swap calldata to an external aggregator, creating a direct price-manipulation and value-extraction surface. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace submit and all relevant address/configuration flows to determine whether swap targets, token paths, minimum output, slippage, deadlines, and recipient constraints are enforced; identify any exploitable condition or conclude that execution is adequately price-protected.

frame_9a52be68fbc1.question: Vulnerability analysis of StakingModule
artifact_refs: Determine whether staking, exit, claim, migration, or plugin accounting can be manipulated to alter the effective price or reward value of TEL
Trace stake checkpoint updates, total-staked calculations, and claimable balances across same-transaction or order-dependent flows
Assess whether externally supplied amounts, token balances, or plugin notifications allow a user to influence pricing-sensitive calculations without adequate invariants

history.rationale: WHY NOW: StakingModule is an unvisited major contract holding the core stake and reward state, and its accounting may define the effective exchange or reward price relied upon by users and plugins. It is therefore the highest-value remaining component for detecting price manipulation beyond the already analyzed FeeBuyback path. EXIT CRITERIA: Review all pricing-sensitive state transitions and views, including stake, exit, claim, migration, plugin registration, and checkpoint logic; map any attacker-controlled inputs and transaction-order dependencies; conclude with either a concrete price-manipulation path and affected invariant or documented evidence that no exploitable price-setting mechanism exists.

frame_d32b92213f74.question: Vulnerability analysis of TieredOwnership
artifact_refs: Determine whether owner or executor transitions can alter price-sensitive FeeBuyback configuration or execution authority
Trace ownership gating for aggregator, safe, TEL, and referral address changes
Check whether nomination, acceptance, or owner-management flows permit unauthorized manipulation of swap parameters or destination addresses

history.rationale: WHY NOW: TieredOwnership is an unvisited permission component that controls owner and executor authority, while FeeBuyback performs externally directed swaps using aggregator and destination configuration. Compromise or unexpected transfer of this authority could enable price manipulation through altered execution parameters or privileged buyback routing. EXIT CRITERIA: Confirm the complete executor/owner transition flow, identify every price-sensitive control reachable through ownership, and establish whether any unauthorized or prematurely effective authority can influence buyback pricing; report a concrete issue only if supported by static code evidence, otherwise mark the component covered.
